risks.message: Row locks (FOR UPDATE/SHARE) only hold inside one transaction; lock and subsequent writes must share the same connection/transaction.

recommendations.message: Keep joins, aggregates, CTEs and bulk DML as parameterized SQL.
Receive an open connection; do not commit inside the function.
Map RAISE EXCEPTION to typed exceptions and RAISE NOTICE to logging.

architectural_decisions.decision: Function receives an open AsyncConnection and never commits; the caller owns the outer transaction.
architectural_decisions.rationale: Row locks (FOR UPDATE) and dependent writes must share one transaction; committing inside would release locks and break atomicity.

architectural_decisions.decision: The PL/pgSQL EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS block is reproduced with conn.begin_nested() (SAVEPOINT): on failure the savepoint is rolled back, the error audit row is inserted, and the error is re-raised.
architectural_decisions.rationale: PL/pgSQL exception handlers run in an implicit subtransaction, so the error log survives even though the failed DML is undone; a plain except on the caller's transaction could not write the log after a failed statement.

architectural_decisions.decision: All SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, UPDATEs and INSERTs remain as parameterized SQL via sqlalchemy.text(); jsonb_build_object is kept in SQL.
architectural_decisions.rationale: Locking, DML and jsonb construction are database concerns; moving them to Python would change locking/atomicity semantics.

architectural_decisions.decision: Each RAISE EXCEPTION maps to a typed exception subclassing TransferenciaError; SQLERRM becomes str(exc).
architectural_decisions.rationale: Typed exceptions allow callers to handle specific failure modes; the generic handler still catches DBAPIError for the audit-log path.

warnings: The error-audit INSERT (TRANSFERENCIA_ERRO) runs on the caller's transaction after the savepoint rollback; if the caller later rolls back the outer transaction, the error log is lost too. In PL/pgSQL the same applies unless the caller committed around the CALL.
The generic 'except Exception' also catches the typed TransferenciaError so the error log is written for validation failures as well, matching WHEN OTHERS; the original error is always re-raised.
SQLERRM in PL/pgSQL is the database error message; str(exc) on a DBAPIError may include Python-side wrapper text, so the 'erro' field in the audit JSON may differ slightly in formatting.
p_valor is typed Decimal | None to mirror NUMERIC(18,2); callers should pass Decimal, not float, to avoid precision drift.
No RAISE NOTICE/INFO/WARNING existed in the routine; logging is used only for the failure path (an addition for observability, not a behaviour change).
